slides.headline: 1) BUY CRYPTO BY TYPING ONE SENTENCE
slides.body:
You type it. It executes. No app switching.

"Buy [$amount] of [coin] on Coinbase at market price."

Grok connects to your wallet and the trade goes through.

slides.headline: 2) SEE YOUR FULL PORTFOLIO IN 3 SECONDS
slides.body:
Ask Grok what you own and it checks your Coinbase account live.

"Show me my Coinbase portfolio. List each coin I own, its current value, and today's gain or loss."

No tab switching.

slides.headline: 3) SET A PRICE ALERT IN PLAIN WORDS
slides.body:
Tell Grok in plain words and it monitors the price live.

"Alert me when Bitcoin drops below $[number] or rises above $[number]. Use my Coinbase data."

You get the notification when it hits.

slides.headline: 4) SEND CRYPTO FROM ONE LINE OF TEXT
slides.body:
One Grok command. No manual steps, no copy-paste errors.

"Send [amount] of [coin] to this wallet: [wallet address]. Use my Coinbase account."

Paste the address in once. Grok handles the rest.

slides.headline: 5) RESEARCH A COIN AND BUY IN THE SAME WINDOW

Three jobs. One window.

pinned_comment: Which one are you trying first? Slide 2 is the one most people can't believe actually works.
editor_override: Slide 4 (price alert) claims Grok 'monitors the price live' and 'you get the notification when it hits' — a proactive push-alert capability that is architecturally distinct from the on-demand query pattern every other slide describes. If the integration does not run a persistent background monitor and push a notification unprompted, this is a false claim that will break the reader's trust the mome
gate_r: s1: The AI-generated face is a textbook wax-figure render — over-smoothed skin, hyperextended grin, glassy eyes — which fails the photo quality bar; the slide reads cleaner as a bold text cover.
